answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per identity to act as a lotus petal in the network, where each node must solve unique puzzles to enter. The verifier checks these against a vast umber ledger of historical results, discarding any duplicates to ensure sybil resistance. While one honest agent pays this base cost, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 distinct puzzles, hitting a rigid wall of processing. Each agent finds its grove in the graph, anchoring work to prevent reuse.
